name: R01 the kept closer is searched again when it is more than 2^20 ahead
why: same answers; quadratic on a line of more than a million characters (30 s against 32 ms at 1,060,200): needs a row with a line longer than 2^20

name: R02 the kept closer is searched again at every opener from index 2^20
why: same answers; quadratic from index 2^20 on (29 s against 35 ms at 1,200,000): needs a row with a line longer than 2^20

name: R03 the kept closer is forgotten after every display region
why: same answers; quadratic on unclosed openers with a display region between them ('$a $$1 b $$1 ' x 8,000: 3.7 s against 12 ms), and quadratic on the parent too, so the row is RED there

name: R04 the same-line test is a backward search for the line break
why: same answers; quadratic with a long line before the closer: 417 ms at the 21,334-opener next-line row (under the limit), 8.9 s at 300,004 characters

name: R05 a blank is a hand-made set, not \s
why: wrong answer on the blanks \s holds that the set leaves out (U+3000, U+2003): no alphabet of the exhaustive or seeded sets holds one

name: R06 a blank leaves out the carriage return
why: wrong answer beside a carriage return ('$a\r$ and $b$'): 51,649 of 2,000,000 diff.js strings differ, but no committed row puts a carriage return beside a dollar

name: R07 a digit is any Unicode decimal digit
why: wrong answer after a closer followed by an Arabic-Indic or a fullwidth digit: no alphabet holds one

name: R08 the line table is one byte an entry
to: new Uint8Array(s.length + 1) as unknown as number[]
why: wrong line past 255 (line 300 reads as 44): no row asks for a region past line 255

name: R09 the line table is two bytes an entry
to: new Uint16Array(s.length + 1) as unknown as number[]
why: wrong line past 65,535 (line 70,000 reads as 4,464): no row asks for a region past line 65,535

name: R10 the kept closer is forgotten at every `$` that cannot open
why: same answers; quadratic on '$a $ ' x 15,000 (5.2 s against 13 ms, 5.2 s on the parent too), where each '$ ' cannot open

name: R11 the closer is searched again once per line when it stands on a later line
to:
if (closer < p + 1 || (closer < s.length && charLine[closer] !== charLine[p] && (scanMathRegions as unknown as { seen?: number }).seen !== charLine[p])) {
          (scanMathRegions as unknown as { seen?: number }).seen = charLine[p];
why: same answers; quadratic on many short lines of openers followed by one closer ('$a $a $a\n' x 10,000 and 'b$': 3.8 s against 49 ms); the parent is linear there, so this is a regression the cure could introduce

name: R12 the escape test reads at most 1,024 backslashes
why: wrong answer for an odd run of more than 1,024 backslashes (an escaped dollar reads as a closer): every row has an even long run or a run of 3

name: R13 the escape test reads at most 64 backslashes
why: wrong answer for an odd run of 65 or more backslashes ('\\' x 65 then '$a$' reads as a region): every row has an even long run or a run of 3
